items.subtype: noun used where an adjective is required
secondary_features: that-clause complement of a factive verb
plural subject-verb agreement inside the that-clause
items.sentence: Field ornithologists have long known that the coastal marshes provide unusually production nesting habitat for migratory shorebirds.
items.error_explanation: The adverb "unusually" premodifies the attributive slot in front of the noun phrase "nesting habitat," and that slot must be filled by an adjective. "Production" is a noun, and an adverb cannot premodify a noun, so the derivational adjective "productive" is required. A is the correct past participle after "have long"; B is the plural noun that licenses the plural verb "provide"; D is the preposition standardly governed by "habitat."

items.subtype: verb form used where a nominal is required
secondary_features: coordinated prepositional phrases governed by depend on
items.sentence: Urban sociologists have argued that neighborhood stability depends less on average income than on the steady expand of local civic institutions.
items.error_explanation: The determiner "the" and the attributive adjective "steady" open a noun phrase that serves as the object of the preposition "on," so the head of that phrase must be a noun. "Expand" is a base-form verb and cannot head a noun phrase, so the deverbal noun "expansion" is required. A is the correct past participle after "have"; B agrees with the singular subject "stability"; C is the correlative standardly required by "less."

items.subtype: past participle required in a reduced relative clause
items.sentence: Fossil trackways excavating from a limestone quarry in southern Utah have persuaded many paleontologists that several large theropods hunted in coordinated groups.
items.error_explanation: The postmodifier attached to "Fossil trackways" is a relative clause reduced from "that were excavated from a limestone quarry," so it requires the past participle of the transitive verb. The present participle "excavating" makes the inanimate trackways the agent and leaves the transitive verb "excavate" with no object, which is not well formed; only the passive past participle "excavated" is possible in this slot. B is a correct attributive adjective, C is the correct past participle inside the present perfect "have persuaded," and D is a correct plural quantified noun phrase.
